verdict.rationale: Logseq's local HTTP API server lets a user create bearer tokens, documented with worked curl examples, so an agent can be given its own credential to the graph. Nothing shows these tokens can be limited to specific methods, graphs, pages, or read-only access, and the single /api endpoint accepts any plugin API method. That makes least-privilege the unproven part of the story. Missing for 10: per-token permission scopes (read-only vs. write, method or graph restrictions), token management and revocation docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
